raw_response:
I've been farming these 3 mu in Quzhou for 30 years now. I'm 50, finished middle school, and I know every corner of my land. My wife and I do most of the work ourselves — our two children work in Shijiazhuang and only come back for the big harvests, so labor is tight. With only 3 mu, every yuan I spend has to be worth it. I can't afford fancy inputs or to gamble on new varieties.

I divide my land into 2 mu for wheat-maize double cropping and 1 mu for cotton. The wheat-maize is my food security — I need that grain. The cotton is my cash, but it's labor hell, and with just my wife and me, I have to be careful not to bite off more than we can chew.

**Winter wheat (2 mu):** I plant around October 10th with an improved local variety. I buy fresh seed — about 8 kg per mu, costs roughly 25 yuan/mu. I don't trust saved seed anymore after I got poor germination three years ago. For fertilizer, the extension agent says I should test my soil, but I know this land. I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then at jointing in March I topdress with another 15 kg or so of urea if the wheat looks a bit yellow. I'd rather put a bit too much than risk a yield drop — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps, and I can't afford to buy grain from the market. I irrigate three times: once at planting if it's dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The well water is metered now, so each irrigation costs me. I spray herbicide once in early spring. I expect about 420 kg/mu if the weather is normal.

**Summer maize (2 mu, same land):** The turnaround after wheat harvest in early June is brutal — sometimes less than a week. I buy hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg/mu, costs around 35 yuan/mu. I have to buy hybrid every year; you can't save it. I put compound fertilizer down at planting — about 45 kg/mu — because I don't have time to come back later. If the season is dry, I irrigate once or twice, usually at the big flare stage and maybe at filling. I spray herbicide and maybe insecticide once if I see pests. I expect about 450 kg/mu.

**Cotton (1 mu):** I plant around April 20th. Seed costs about 30 yuan/mu. I put down about 35 kg of compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress with urea at flowering. Cotton needs spraying — I usually do 3 or 4 sprays for bollworm and aphids, which is my biggest input cost for this crop. I irrigate twice if it's dry. Picking is all by hand, spread across September and October. My wife and I do most of it, and the children help during the National Day holiday. I expect about 260 kg/mu of seed cotton. It's only 1 mu, but the price has been decent, so it brings in needed cash.

Total input cost for the year is about 1,050 yuan. That's a lot for a smallholder like me, but I can't cut much more without risking my family's grain and income.
